title: What Matters When Building Universal Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Models?
abstract: arXiv:2601.06347v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Recent progress in universal multilingual named entity recognition (NER) has been driven by multilingual transformer models, task-specific architectures, custom loss functions, and large-scale training datasets. However, despite substantial prior work, we find that many design decisions for such models are made without systematic justification, with individual components evaluated only in combination rather than in isolation. We argue that this impedes progress in the field by making it difficult to identify which choices improve multilingual generalization. In this work, we conduct an extensive empirical evaluation on transformer backbones, architectures, training objectives, data composition, and threshold selection for zero-shot, multilingual NER models. translated_title: 构建通用多语言命名实体识别模型时，什么才是关键？
translated_abstract: 近来通用多语言命名实体识别（NER）的进展主要由多语言Transformer模型、任务特定架构、自定义损失函数以及大规模训练数据集所推动。然而，尽管已有大量先前工作，我们发现许多模型设计决策缺乏系统性的论证，各个组件仅在组合状态下被评估，而非单独评估。我们认为这阻碍了该领域的进展，因为难以识别哪些选择能够改善多语言泛化能力。在本工作中，我们针对零样本多语言NER模型的Transformer骨干网络、架构、训练目标、数据组成和阈值选择进行了广泛的实证评估。基于这些发现，我们提出了Otter——一个小型编码器模型，它在强大的多语言NER基线之上取得了一致的性能提升，超越了同等规模的模型。
tldr: 本文系统性评估了多语言NER模型中各组件设计选择的影响，并提出小型编码器模型Otter，在零样本多语言NER任务上持续超越同等规模的强基线模型。
en_tdlr: Through extensive empirical evaluation of design choices in multilingual NER, we propose Otter, a small encoder model that consistently outperforms similarly sized strong baselines on zero-shot multilingual NER.
